meta.title: DNS Mesh Protocol
meta.description: Send end-to-end encrypted messages over DNS — the same network that resolves every domain name. No central server, no app store, no gatekeeper.

hero.title: Encrypted email, delivered by the same lookup that finds google.com.
hero.lede: DNS Mesh carries end-to-end encrypted messages between two people over ordinary DNS — no relay company in the middle, no app store, no account to sign up for.

ledger.label: Protocol facts
ledger.lookups: TXT lookups carry a whole conversation

anchor.label: mental model
anchor.text: Think of it as federated email — only it rides on DNS instead of SMTP.

i.title: Identity
i.body: A name in DNS, not in an app store. Bob asks who Alice is and her domain answers with public TXT records holding her long-term keys (Ed25519 for signing, X25519 for key exchange).

ii.title: Mailbox slots
ii.body: Alice leaves a note in her own public mailbox saying a message for Bob is waiting and where its chunks live. She writes with signed UPDATEs; anyone reads back plain TXT.

iii.title: Ciphertext
iii.body: The contents travel encrypted — chunked, signed via RFC 8945 TSIG, written with RFC 2136 DNS UPDATE. The recursive chain only ever sees opaque bytes.

prose.title: Reads are open. Writes are signed.
prose.p1: That asymmetry is what removes the gatekeeper.
prose.metaphor: Think of a mailbox on a public street: anyone walking by can read the address, but only the person with the key can drop something inside.
prose.p2: On any network, anyone can resolve a user’s identity, mailbox slots, and chunks — they’re public TXT records served by ordinary DNS. Writes are different: they’re RFC 2136 DNS UPDATE packets signed with an RFC 8945 TSIG key issued per user.
prose.p3: A single HTTPS call mints that key on first registration. After that, no HTTPS hop is involved in publishing identity, refreshing prekeys, or delivering chunks — it’s DNS the whole way down. Every node in the federation accepts those signed updates from any user whose key it has on file, which means no single node is canonical and none of them can hold a conversation hostage.

try.title: Five minutes against the public node.
try.intro: The reference node at dnsmesh.io has open registration and provides the bootstrap-seed and claim-provider roles other nodes default to — so anyone can try DMP without standing anything up. Self-hosting gets the same capabilities; both modes interoperate over DNS, because the wire is the contract.

warn.label: notice
warn.lead: The protocol has not been externally audited yet.
warn.body: Wire format, federation, identity, key rotation, and the formal spec have all shipped — the cryptographic audit has not. Until it lands, don’t route confidentiality-critical traffic through DMP. Read
warn.tail: before trusting this with anything that matters.

footer.tagline: End-to-end encrypted messages, delivered over DNS. Open protocol, no gatekeeper.
